verses.text: Balaam was sure that the LORD would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the LORD wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!

footnotes.text: my words are true: One possible meaning for the difficult Hebrew text.

verses.text: It comes from the LORD, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
“People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the LORD has planted, or like cedars growing near water.

footnotes.text: grove of palm trees: Or “green valley.”

verses.text: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.

footnotes.text: Agag the Amalekite: The Amalekites were longtime enemies of the Israelites (see Exodus 17.8-16), and Agag was one of their most powerful kings.

verses.text: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.

footnotes.text: shooting them with arrows: One possible meaning for the difficult Hebrew text.

verses.text: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the LORD didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
Balaam answered, “I told your messengers
that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the LORD. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.”
Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!

footnotes.text: my words are true: One possible meaning for the difficult Hebrew text.

verses.text: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the LORD All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
“What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.

footnotes.text: you Moabites: Or “the territories of Moab.”
destroy: The Standard Hebrew Text; the Samaritan Hebrew Text “the skulls of.”
those tribes … desert: The Hebrew text has “the descendants of Sheth,” which probably refers to the people who lived in the desert areas of Canaan before the Israelites.

verses.text: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.

footnotes.text: every town there: Or “Ir in Moab.”

verses.text: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.

footnotes.text: the Amalekites: See the note at 24.7.
but … forever: One possible meaning for the difficult Hebrew text.

verses.text: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,

footnotes.text: the Kenites: A group of people who lived in the desert south of Israel.

verses.text: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.

footnotes.text: them: One possible meaning for the difficult Hebrew text of verse 22.

verses.text: “No one can survive if God plans destruction.

footnotes.text: destruction: One possible meaning for the difficult Hebrew text of verse 23.

verses.text: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
